question: Can the Korean cultivated vegetable name 아욱 be mapped to a species-level identity without treating every plant called mallow as interchangeable?

conclusion.reason: Authoritative Korean agricultural resources consistently map the cultivated vegetable 아욱 to Malva verticillata. This resolves the Korean crop-name identity question, but does not make Malva spp. a species-level identity and does not by itself establish tortoise feeding suitability.

sources.crop_context: cultivated vegetable; young leaves and stems harvested
sources.supports: Species-level identity of the Korean cultivated crop 아욱.
sources.does_not_support: Tortoise safety, feeding frequency, captive diet role, or identity of every product/weed marketed under a generic mallow name.

sources.supports: Independent Korean agricultural-resource corroboration of the crop-name mapping.
sources.does_not_support: A genus-wide Malva feeding verdict or tortoise-specific safety.

sources.authority: Royal Botanic Gardens, Kew - Plants of the World Online
sources.distribution_context: native range extends across temperate Asia including Korea
sources.supports: International taxonomic backbone for the species name.

tortoise_evidence_context.interpretation: Direct evidence for another Malva species in another T. graeca subspecies. It is related-species context only and cannot be transferred as exact evidence for M. verticillata.

exact_species_literature_review.search_scope: Malva verticillata combined with Testudo, tortoise, chelonian, feeding, toxicology, nitrate, oxalate and phytochemistry terms; primary literature prioritized.
exact_species_literature_review.interpretation: No peer-reviewed exact-species evidence was verified in this pass showing Testudo graeca ibera or another Testudo taxon consuming Malva verticillata. Absence of a located paper is not evidence that tortoises cannot eat the plant.
exact_species_literature_review.do_not_infer: Do not transfer Malva parviflora feeding observations to M. verticillata and do not convert human edibility into a tortoise feeding verdict.

rda_candidate_record.note: Ca:P is calculated from reported Ca and P values and is descriptive only. These values must be reconciled against the official RDA workbook already supplied to the project before canonical nutrition publication.

phytochemistry_context.title: Chemical profiling of Malva verticillata L. by UPLC-Q-TOF-MSE and their antioxidant activity in vitro
phytochemistry_context.finding: Nineteen compounds were preliminarily identified and phenolic content was measured in extracts; leaves had the highest reported total phenolic content among the tested parts.
phytochemistry_context.does_not_support: Tortoise safety, oxalate burden, nitrate burden, feeding frequency, or captive diet role.

phytochemistry_context.title: Cardioprotective effect of Malva verticillata against doxorubicin-induced toxicity in rats
phytochemistry_context.finding: Phytochemical screening reported alkaloids, saponins, phenols, flavonoids, ash and tannins in the tested methanolic leaf extract.
phytochemistry_context.method_context: Leaves were dried, powdered and methanol-extracted; the biological experiment used rats and an extract rather than intact leaves.
phytochemistry_context.does_not_support: Whole-leaf tortoise safety, antinutrient dose, or a captive feeding recommendation.

phytochemistry_context.title: Origin of sennosides in health teas including Malva leaves
phytochemistry_context.finding: Sennosides A and B were not detected in Malva verticillata leaves; sennosides in sampled commercial teas were attributed to senna material.
phytochemistry_context.supports: Rejects the specific hypothesis that M. verticillata leaf itself contains sennosides A/B in the tested context.
phytochemistry_context.does_not_support: General tortoise safety, feeding frequency, nitrate or oxalate safety, or absence of other potentially relevant compounds.

hazard_review.nitrate_note: Secondary plant databases repeat a warning that nitrogen-rich cultivation can increase leaf nitrate, but no sufficiently direct primary exact-species nitrate study relevant to tortoise feeding was verified in this pass. Do not publish a quantitative nitrate limit from this material.
hazard_review.sennoside_note: Kojima et al. 2001 directly tested M. verticillata leaves and did not detect sennosides A or B. This resolves only that narrow compound question and is not a whole-plant safety test.
hazard_review.rule: Do not infer oxalate or nitrate burden from other Malva species or generic leafy-green assumptions. Do not infer whole-leaf tortoise safety from extract pharmacology, human edibility, or absence of sennosides A/B.

required_database_rule: If the public entry means Korean cultivated 아욱, its identity may be represented as Malva verticillata L. with the Korean crop sources above. If the entry intentionally means generic mallow/Malva spp., keep it genus-level and identity-blocked for species-specific claims. Do not change the feeding verdict solely from identity, human food composition, extract phytochemistry, absence of sennosides A/B, or related-species feeding evidence.
next_required_evidence: Exact Malva verticillata feeding or toxicology evidence relevant to chelonians/herbivorous reptiles
Primary exact-species nitrate and oxalate data for edible leaves if available
Official RDA workbook reconciliation for raw 아욱 nutrient values
Migration plan separating Korean cultivated 아욱 from generic Malva spp. without misidentifying existing generic records
